answer: Resist sybils with karst bonding: each new identity locks non-refundable stake that sinks into a shared pool for one full epoch before any vote counts. Peers watch attestation graphs; a sudden ripple of near-identical answers or mutual-attest cliques from fresh keys triggers proportional slash of that locked stake. Surviving agents join a grove of cross-signed vouchers where each endorsement risks the voucherer's own bond, so cloning identities costs both capital and peer trust faster than rewards accrue.
